concepts.name: Quadratic Equations
concepts.description: A quadratic equation is a polynomial equation of degree two that can be written in the standard form ax² + bx + c = 0, where a ≠ 0. Such equations arise in geometry, algebra, and real-life applications involving areas, motion, and optimization.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify quadratic equations and express them in standard form.

concepts.name: Standard Form and Components
concepts.description: The coefficients a, b, and c determine the characteristics of a quadratic equation. Understanding these components is essential for selecting appropriate solution methods.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify the coefficients and constant term of a quadratic equation.

concepts.name: Formation of Quadratic Equations
concepts.description: Quadratic equations can be formed from algebraic expressions and real-life situations involving geometric measurements, product relationships, and numerical conditions.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to formulate quadratic equations from mathematical statements and word problems.

concepts.name: Verification of Solutions
concepts.description: A solution of a quadratic equation is verified by substituting it into the original equation and checking whether it satisfies the equality.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to verify whether a given value is a solution of a quadratic equation.

topics.title: Solution of a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation

concepts.name: Factorisation Method
concepts.description: The factorisation method solves quadratic equations by expressing the quadratic polynomial as a product of two linear factors and applying the zero-product property.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to solve quadratic equations using the factorisation method.

concepts.name: Zero Product Property
concepts.description: If the product of two algebraic factors is zero, then at least one of the factors must be zero. This principle forms the basis of solving factorised quadratic equations.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to apply the zero-product property to determine the roots of quadratic equations.

concepts.name: Applications of Factorisation
concepts.description: Many real-world mathematical problems can be converted into quadratic equations and solved efficiently using factorisation when suitable factors exist.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to solve contextual problems involving quadratic equations using factorisation.

concepts.name: Discriminant
concepts.description: The discriminant (b² − 4ac) determines the nature of the roots of a quadratic equation without solving it. It indicates whether the roots are real, equal, distinct, or imaginary.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to calculate the discriminant and determine the nature of the roots of a quadratic equation.

concepts.name: Types of Roots
concepts.description: Quadratic equations may have two distinct real roots, one repeated real root, or no real roots depending on the value of the discriminant.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to classify the roots of quadratic equations based on the discriminant.

concepts.name: Relationship Between Graph and Roots
concepts.description: The number of points where the graph of a quadratic function intersects the x-axis corresponds to the number of real roots of the quadratic equation.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to relate the graphical representation of a quadratic function to the nature of its roots.

concepts.name: Key Concepts of Quadratic Equations
concepts.description: This chapter consolidates the identification, formation, factorisation, and analysis of quadratic equations along with determining the nature of their roots.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to select appropriate methods to solve quadratic equations and interpret the significance of their roots in mathematical and real-world contexts.
